title: Missed nursing care and shift-level staffing shortfalls on adult inpatient units: a cross-sectional survey linked to scheduling records
abstract: Objective: to estimate the prevalence of missed nursing care and its association with below-plan staffing of the shift described, adjusted for acuity. Design: cross-sectional last-shift survey of registered and licensed practical nurses on 18 units, linked to scheduling and acuity records. Primary outcome: any of 22 activities missed on the last shift. Results and conclusions will be written after analysis.
introduction: Nurses report that care is left undone when shifts are short, but published studies disagree on whether acuity explains the association, and most rely on nurses' recall of their staffing. This study links each report to the recorded hours and acuity of the shift described.
methods: All eligible nurses were invited to complete a pretested 22-item checklist during paid time. Each response was linked to actual and planned hours and to unit acuity on the shift described. A mixed-effects logistic model with a unit random intercept estimated the association.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present response by role and shift, item-level prevalence, and unadjusted and acuity-adjusted associations.
discussion: The discussion will compare the findings with the retrieved shift-level and multi-hospital studies and with the undated conflicting abstract. It will set out what the figures mean for the budget round without attributing missed care to individual nurses.
limitations: Missed care is self-reported and acuity is a unit mean for the day. The study covers one hospital in one winter, and the instrument is not validated for licensed practical nurses.
conclusion: To be written after analysis. It will describe associations and will not attribute missed care to individual nurses.
summary: STROBE-structured draft; results left empty until the survey closes.
